title: Open Muse and send your first message
summary: Muse is Meta’s personal AI agent. Start with one small request that needs only the words you type.
where: On an iPad, enter muse.ai in Safari, or get Muse from Meta in the App Store. The US listing rates it 18+ and requires iPadOS 18 or later.
On Windows use muse.ai. Meta also offers a Mac app, an iPhone app and an Android app. Sign in with a Meta account in a supported country. Free usage has a limit that refreshes.

actions.title: Find the right service
actions.do: Type muse.ai into the address bar. Select the entry to try Muse, or open the official app.
actions.see: You reach Meta sign-in or your Muse conversation.
actions.stuck: Check the app publisher and local availability. The US and Australia have launched. Your local store and Muse sign-in show access where you live.

actions.title: Open Chat
actions.do: Sign in with your eligible Meta account and follow the setup screens. Open Chat.
actions.see: A message box appears at the bottom of the chat.
actions.stuck: Skip optional connections. Sorting words that you type requires no mailbox access.

actions.title: Send a tiny request
actions.do: Send “Put these stops in alphabetical order: Berlin, Aachen, Dresden.”
actions.see: The reply should read Aachen, Berlin, Dresden.
actions.stuck: If you see suggested tasks, return to Chat and look for the message box.

actions.title: Make one correction
actions.do: Send “Add Bremen and sort again.”
actions.see: Aachen, Berlin, Bremen, Dresden appear in that order.
actions.stuck: If a stop is missing, paste all four names together and ask for the count.

roles: Sketch a tiny alphabetical app index.
sources: Apple · Muse from Meta, compatibility and age rating
Meta · download Muse for your device
Meta · the launch of Muse in Australia

title: Give Muse a small planning job
summary: Practice asking a follow-up while keeping a personal project together in one conversation.
where: Open muse.ai or the Muse app and choose Chat. A side chat is a separate thread for a particular subject.

actions.title: Start a side chat
actions.do: Open the menu at the upper left of Chat, then choose the pencil for a new side chat.
actions.see: A fresh conversation opens.
actions.stuck: Use the main Chat if the side-chat button has moved. The exercise only needs a conversation.

actions.title: Give it three fixed facts
actions.do: Send “My ferry leaves at 10:30. Boarding closes 20 minutes earlier. Walking to the dock takes 15 minutes. Calculate my latest walking departure.”
actions.see: Latest boarding is 10:10. Latest walking departure is 09:55.
actions.stuck: If it suggests a cushion, ask for the exact clock times first.

actions.title: Change one assumption
actions.do: Send “Allow a 10-minute cushion before boarding closes. Keep the ferry and walking time.”
actions.see: Your walking departure moves to 09:45.
actions.stuck: If the sailing moves, remind Muse that its time is fixed.

actions.title: Keep the result together
actions.do: Request three lines labeled Leave, Arrive and Boarding closes. Reopen this thread from the chat list.
actions.see: The three times are 09:45, 10:00 and 10:10.
actions.stuck: Look for the most recent exchange. Side chats organize topics; Muse can still draw on other chats.

roles: Calculate a sample maintenance notice deadline.
Create test times for a countdown app.

title: See what Muse can read or change
summary: A connector is a link to another service. Learn to read its permission screen before choosing what to share.
where: Open Muse, then Settings. You can inspect the connector list and try a sample calendar task without signing in to another service.

actions.title: Find the list
actions.do: Select Connectors. Choose an available calendar connector and read the next screen. Stop before authorizing access.
actions.see: The screen names the service and describes the requested connection.
actions.stuck: If the calendar is absent, inspect another connector or open the official connector guide.

actions.title: Tell reading from writing
actions.do: Look for a permission to view events and one that would let an app create or change them.
actions.see: Viewing permits reading a date. Creating could add an event to a calendar.
actions.stuck: If access is bundled, leave the connection unopened and use the sample below.

actions.title: Try the task by hand
actions.do: Return to Chat and send “Sample rehearsal June 8, 13:00–13:30. Draft a reminder 10 minutes before it starts. Show only the text.”
actions.see: The draft proposes 12:50 on June 8.
actions.stuck: Ask for the exact minute. A draft does not establish that a calendar entry exists.

actions.title: Locate approval controls
actions.do: Open Settings and select Permissions. Inspect the choices for connectors.
actions.see: When Muse requests approval, See task details explains what it proposes.
actions.stuck: Decline any unexpected request and return to your draft.

roles: Draft a reminder using sample mail text.
Compare calendar reading with calendar editing.
Design a clear permission request for an app.
sources: Meta · connecting or disconnecting a service

title: Schedule a one-time reminder and check delivery
summary: A scheduled task lets Muse return to a request later. Check its schedule and its eventual message separately.
where: Open Chat in Muse. Choose a time about ten minutes ahead on your clock.

actions.title: Ask for one reminder
actions.do: Send “Remind me once today at [your time and time zone] to check the packing list.” Fill in the brackets first.
actions.see: Muse should repeat your reminder and time.
actions.stuck: If the day or zone is wrong, correct it now.

actions.title: Check the schedule
actions.do: Tap your assistant icon at the top, select Upcoming and open the reminder.
actions.see: Its time, date and one-time setting match your request.
actions.stuck: If it is missing, ask which reminders are scheduled. A sentence promising to remind you is only the first check.

actions.title: Check after the set time
actions.do: Return to Muse a little after the due time. Look for the message in Chat.
actions.see: A delivered message confirms it ran. A device notification may also appear if enabled.
actions.stuck: If there was no alert, check the chat first, then the scheduled time and device notification settings.

actions.title: Check for accidental repeats
actions.do: Ask which future reminders remain for the packing list. If it repeats, cancel that one item and verify Upcoming.
actions.see: There should be no future recurring practice reminder.
actions.stuck: Match the label and time before canceling.

roles: Rehearse a reminder to check a sample report.
Follow up on a practice checklist.
Observe the difference between scheduled and delivered.

title: Make a packing-list file and find it again
summary: Muse calls a file it creates an artifact. Make one, revise it, and check the saved copy.
where: Open Muse Chat. The Library tab holds files and finished work. You can do this exercise with three words you supply.

actions.title: Request a file
actions.do: Send “Create a plain-text file named Dock List with three lines: passport, cabin key, charger.”
actions.see: A finished file appears in the conversation.
actions.stuck: If the answer is a text bubble, request a plain-text file saved to Library.

actions.title: Open the saved copy
actions.do: Open Library and select the file with Dock List in its name.
actions.see: You should see all three items.
actions.stuck: You can also open the file from the original chat message.

actions.title: Give one edit
actions.do: Send “In that same Dock List file, replace charger with USB cable. Keep the other two items.”
actions.see: The updated file should still have three lines.
actions.stuck: If two files exist, open the file attached to the latest edit reply and check its name.

actions.title: Verify the contents
actions.do: Close the file, reopen it from Library and read its three lines.
actions.see: Passport, cabin key and USB cable appear. Charger is gone.
actions.stuck: If the old word remains, quote it and ask which file was edited.

roles: Draft sample text for a packing app.

title: Create a picture and request one precise edit
summary: Try Muse’s built-in image skill on a design you can inspect at a glance.
where: Open a Muse conversation. Image creation is a built-in skill. Your remaining allowance can affect whether your request runs.

actions.title: Describe the picture
actions.do: Send “Make a square image of one red mug on a plain cream table. Draw one blue star on the mug. No words.”
actions.see: You receive an image you can open.
actions.stuck: If you only see a description, ask for an actual generated image file.

actions.title: Count the details
actions.do: Open the picture and count the mugs and stars. Check the frame shape.
actions.see: One mug, one blue star and a square frame are your tests.
actions.stuck: Correct one detail at a time. Keep the original handy for comparison.

actions.title: Edit one feature
actions.do: Send “Keep the composition. Change only the mug color to green.”
actions.see: The mug changes while the star, table and frame stay alike.
actions.stuck: If the scene changes completely, refer to the earlier image or attach it again.

actions.title: Choose a version
actions.do: Open the newer picture, look at it at a small size and check Library for saved work.
actions.see: You can judge which version remains recognizable as a small icon.
actions.stuck: If you reach a usage limit, keep the prompt and retry after the allowance refreshes.

roles: Sketch an illustration for a training note.
Draft artwork for an Office how-to.
Try an icon concept for a personal app.
